svg.title: Watermarks and reclaim
svg.desc: Free memory in a zone against its three watermarks, from /proc/zoneinfo of a 2 GB Ubuntu 24.04 VM: min 5632 pages (22 MiB), low 7040 (27.5 MiB), high 8448 (33 MiB). Above high, kswapd sleeps. When free memory falls below low, kswapd wakes and reclaims in the background until free memory is back above high. Below min, a process that allocates has to reclaim pages itself: direct reclaim, and it stalls. If nothing can be reclaimed, the OOM killer runs. One 2.2 GiB allocation on that VM: kswapd scanned 752946 pages and freed 391995, direct reclaim scanned 245942 and freed 18833, PSI memory recorded 0.13 s of stall, and sar showed 82 percent vmeff in the busiest second.
svg.text: Free memory vs the zone watermarks: who reclaims, and when
free memory in the zone (not to scale)
high
8448 pages
low
7040 pages
min
5632 pages
33 MiB
27.5 MiB
22 MiB
kswapd sleeps
Allocations are served from free memory; nothing to do.
kswapd keeps going
Once woken, kswapd reclaims until free memory is back above high,
so it stops with some headroom instead of waking again at once.
Below low: kswapd wakes (background reclaim)
Drops clean cache, writes dirty pages, swaps out inactive anonymous
memory, shrinks slab. Programs keep running. Counted as pgscan_kswapd.
Below min: direct reclaim
kswapd can't keep up. The process that asks for memory reclaims pages
itself before the allocation succeeds, and stalls while it does.
Counted as pgscan_direct, and as stall time in /proc/pressure/memory.
Nothing left to reclaim: OOM killer
The kernel kills the process with the highest oom_score.
One 2.2 GiB allocation on the 2 GB VM (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, 2 GiB swap)
kswapd: scanned 752946 pages, freed 391995. Direct reclaim: scanned 245942, freed 18833. PSI memory: 0.13 s of stall (some ≈ full).
sar -B, busiest second: pgscank/s 738647, pgscand/s 243507, pgsteal/s 806566, %vmeff 82.12. low − min = 1408 pages = min / 4.
